official_statement_rationale: With headline CPI inflation at 7.01 per cent, we have breached the upper tolerance limit for six consecutive months. The persistence of inflation, particularly the stickiness of core inflation at 6.20 per cent, signals that price pressures are becoming generalized and risk unanchoring inflation expectations. A positive output gap of 0.40 per cent and a systemic liquidity surplus of 190,000 crore INR provide the necessary space for a front-loaded policy response. Given the headwinds from global commodity prices and the pressures on the USD/INR exchange rate, a 50 basis point hike is imperative to demonstrate our commitment to price stability and to prevent the entrenchment of second-round effects. Anything less than a decisive adjustment risks falling behind the curve, ultimately necessitating more painful policy actions in the future.
